exercise: Lesson 3 Neural Networks - Sprint 02 Regression MLP Baseline
cell_or_location: train function call, cell 5 -> train cell 3 line 10, outputs = model(batch_x)
error_message: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (1x32 and 1x10)
what_user_was_trying: Pass a batch of scalar x values through an MLP whose first layer is nn.Linear(1, 10).
real_cause: The DataLoader produced batch_x with shape [32]. A reshape call was attempted but not assigned, and reshape(1, -1) would have made one sample with 32 features instead of 32 samples with one feature.
user_diagnosis_steps: Printed batch_x.shape inside the training loop and connected the linear layer's in_features=1 to the required last dimension of the input tensor.
user_fix: Assigned the reshaped tensor inside the loop with batch_x = batch_x.reshape(-1, 1), so each batch becomes [batch_size, 1] before model(batch_x).
memory_rule: For nn.Linear(in_features, ...), the last input dimension must equal in_features; use [batch_size, features], not [features] or [1, batch_size]. Also remember reshape returns a new tensor unless assigned.
next_drill: Check loss inputs too: for MSELoss, outputs and targets should intentionally have compatible shapes; avoid accidental broadcasting between outputs shaped [batch_size, 1] and targets shaped [batch_size].

memory_rule: A neural net can run while still learning the wrong thing; treat PyTorch loss-shape warnings as hard failures until output and target shapes match intentionally.

exercise: Lesson 3 Neural Networks - Sprint 02 Regression MLP Baseline
error_message: Loss initially dropped, then jumped and plateaued when Adam used lr=0.1.
what_user_was_trying: Make the sin(x) MLP learn after the dtype and shape bugs were fixed.
real_cause: Adam learning rate 0.1 was too high, making training unstable. The printed value was also the last batch loss, so the log looked noisier than a true epoch-average curve.
user_diagnosis_steps: Compared the loss trajectory: it decreased from about 0.60 to about 0.08, then jumped above 0.20, which indicated unstable learning rather than a dead training loop.

memory_rule: If neural-network loss drops then suddenly gets worse, suspect learning-rate instability first; for Adam baselines, start around 1e-3 before changing architecture.

error_message: Expected all tensors to be on the same device, but got mat1 is on cpu, different from other tensors on cuda:0 (when checking argument in method wrapper_CUDA_addmm)
what_user_was_trying: Train a binary classifier on the two-moons dataset with the model on CUDA and full-batch tensors passed into a custom train function.
real_cause: The model was moved to CUDA, but x_train.to(device) and y_train.to(device) were called without assignment. For regular tensors, .to(device) returns a new tensor instead of mutating in place, so the forward pass still used CPU inputs against CUDA weights.
user_diagnosis_steps: Checked the traceback location at model(x_train), compared tensor and model devices, and inspected whether the returned tensors from .to(device) were being reassigned.
user_fix: Reassigned the moved tensors inside train with x_train = x_train.to(device) and y_train = y_train.to(device).reshape(-1, 1) before the forward pass.
memory_rule: In PyTorch, tensor.to(device) does not move a plain tensor in place; always reassign and verify model, inputs, and targets are on the same device before the first forward pass.
next_drill: Before training, print x_train.device, y_train.device, and next(model.parameters()).device, then intentionally fix one mismatch without changing anything else.

error_message: Reported accuracy stayed 0.0 for all epochs while loss kept decreasing.
what_user_was_trying: Measure binary-classification accuracy on the two-moons test set during training with BCEWithLogitsLoss.
real_cause: The metric compares y_test values 0/1 against raw logits from model(X_test). Logits are unconstrained real numbers, so exact equality with class labels is almost never true, making the computed accuracy collapse to 0 even when the model is learning.
user_diagnosis_steps: Observed that loss decreased steadily while acc remained exactly 0.0, then inspected the accuracy expression and compared its inputs to the BCEWithLogitsLoss training contract.
memory_rule: For BCEWithLogitsLoss, logits are not class labels. Convert logits to probabilities with sigmoid and threshold, or threshold logits directly at 0, before computing accuracy.

real_cause: The test input was reshaped with reshape(1, -1), turning 200 scalar samples into one sample with 200 features. The model's first layer is nn.Linear(1, 10), so it expects the last dimension of batch_x to stay 1.
user_diagnosis_steps: Read the traceback at model(batch_x), compared the failing shape (1x200) against the first layer contract nn.Linear(1, 10), and checked the difference between the training reshape and the evaluation reshape.
user_fix: Changed the evaluation-side reshape so the test input keeps the scalar-feature layout instead of flipping into one wide row.
memory_rule: For nn.Linear(1, ...), scalar regression inputs must stay shaped [batch_size, 1] in both training and evaluation. If a reshape changes them to [1, batch_size], the layer will treat the batch as features and fail.
